To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) skilled performers use automatic processes for the transformation of perceptual information into motor output, and (2) controlled processes are used for the transformation of information into automatic processes and for the control of the performance system.
(1) automatic processing is modular and (2) the development of automatic processing is the result of consistent practice.
Automatic processes are modular, fast, accurate, coordinated, resource-free and show high transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and maintenance of skill.
the development of automatic processing in skilled performance and the development and maintenance of control processing in motor skills.
understanding how attention develops with practice and how it relates to the development of skill.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of skilled motor performance involves a change from a controlled process to an automatic process.
attention theory and mechanisms for skilled performance are currently undergoing a major reorganization and that the implications for the motor skill literature are profound.

attention theory and mechanisms for skilled performance are not well defined, but the current state of the research suggests that a dual process theory of automatic and controlled processing may be a fruitful approach for future research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
skilled motor performance involves the use of automatic processing and controlled processing.
automatic processing develops with practice, is resource free, and is not under direct control.
skilled performance is a result of the development of automatic processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to understand how the brain learns and how we can apply this knowledge to improve the learning and retention of motor skills.

the development of automatic processing is an important factor in the development of expertise and that the current theory of attention provides a useful framework for the study of skilled performance.
attention is a dynamic, multi-dimensional construct that can be used to explain a wide range of phenomena.
